findings.observation: Examined Sheet 13 (Overall Site & Paving & Striping Plan) using the vision tool. The sheet acts as a land use map by explicitly labeling all adjacent properties with their zoning designations and current land uses. To the west: SF-3 (office use), MF-4 (apartment/condo), P (government services). To the north: CS (apartment/condo, office). To the east: CS-V (commercial). To the south: CS MU-V-CO and MF-4 (apartment/condo). The Consolidated Site Plan Application Section 10 confirms the site is subject to Compatibility Standards.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires a land use map showing adjacent land uses when the site is subject to Compatibility Standards. Since the CC Application confirms applicability and Sheet 13 provides both zoning labels and use descriptions for all adjacent properties (including the triggering SF-3 residential property to the west), the deficiency described in CMP-01 (map not provided) does not exist. The sheet provides the required information to demonstrate compliance with LDC 25-2-1051-1063.
findings.explanation: Sheet 13 provides a land use map with adjacent property zoning (SF-3, MF-4, CS, CS-V, CS MU-V-CO, P) and uses (single family, apartment/condo, commercial, office, government services) clearly labeled.

findings.observation: Examined Sheets 35 and 36 (Building Elevations) using the vision tool. Sheet 35 shows North and East building elevations. Sheet 36 shows South and West elevations. Both sheets include a Material Legend with six materials: Fiber Cement Board Painted, Metal Panel, King Brick, Wood Tone Fiber Cement, Glass, and Living Wall. The elevations display extensive architectural details including fenestration patterns, balconies with railings, storefronts, structural columns, amenity decks, varying rooflines, and material articulation. Sheet 35 also includes a Glazed Opening Schedule with specifications for window types A through E and S1, and a Compatibility Diagram showing height restrictions.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires building elevations showing architectural elements when subject to Compatibility Standards. The elevations on Sheets 35 and 36 clearly show architectural elements including materials, finishes, windows, doors, balconies, and facade articulation. The material legend and glazed opening schedule provide additional detail about the architectural character. This satisfies the requirement for demonstrating architectural elements as part of compatibility review, so the deficiency described in CMP-02 (elevations not provided) does not exist.
findings.explanation: Sheets 35 and 36 provide four building elevations (North, East, South, West) with detailed architectural elements including material legend, fenestration, balconies, finishes, and glazed opening schedule.

findings.observation: Examined Sheet 14 (Dimensional Control & Site Plan 1 of 2) using the vision tool. The sheet shows compatibility setback lines drawn parallel to the western property line adjacent to properties labeled 'ZONING: SF-3' and 'USE: SINGLE FAMILY'. Four setback lines are labeled: 15' Compatibility Setback Line, 25' Compatibility Setback Line, 50' Compatibility Setback Line, and 75' Compatibility Setback Line. A table titled 'COMPATIBILITY SETBACK LINES' specifies allowable building heights by distance: 0'-10' (0' Screening Zone), 10'-25' (0' Restricted Zone), 25'-50' (40'), 50'-75' (60'). Sheet 35 also includes a Compatibility Diagram - North showing height restrictions relative to the property line.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires setbacks adjacent to residential uses or zoning to be shown on plans when subject to Compatibility Standards. Sheet 14 graphically depicts compatibility setback lines at 15', 25', 50', and 75' distances from the SF-3 residential property line, accompanied by a table detailing height restrictions for each zone. This clearly demonstrates where setbacks apply and what restrictions govern development near the triggering residential property. The deficiency described in CMP-03 (setbacks not shown) does not exist.
findings.explanation: Sheet 14 shows compatibility setback lines (15', 25', 50', 75') adjacent to SF-3 residential zoning with a table specifying height restrictions: 0' for 0'-50' zones, 40' for 50'-75' zone.

summary: All 3 items pass. The site is subject to Compatibility Standards, and all required documentation is provided: land use map with adjacent zoning/uses on Sheet 13, building elevations with architectural elements on Sheets 35-36, and compatibility setbacks adjacent to SF-3 residential zoning on Sheet 14.
